answer: One defence is Wax renderer honey jar assay sealed by the nectar charter: each honey jar is a brood record countersigned by the inspector, so a farm must render a hundred real wax blocks by hand, and the velvet of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the plume of those crossings is a bill no payout covers. The thread is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
